Lemma
[Extensions of an Injection to a Permutation]

Every injection $j \colon \iota _a \to \iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$ is the restriction to the $\iota _a$-summand of exactly $l!$ permutations of $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$. Consequently, for every function $G$ from maps $\iota _a \to \iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$ into a commutative monoid, vanishing on the non-injective maps, \[ \sum _{\sigma \in S_{\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b}} G\big(\sigma |_{\iota _a}\big) \; =\; l! \sum _{j \colon \iota _a \to \iota _a \sqcup \iota _b} G(j), \] the right-hand sum running over all maps.
Proof

First, one extension exists: the complement of the range of $j$ in $\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b$ has cardinality $(k+l) - k = l$, so there is a bijection $\psi $ of $\iota _b$ onto it, and the map equal to $j$ on $\iota _a$ and to $\psi $ on $\iota _b$ is a permutation extending $j$. Next, the extensions of $j$ form a left coset $\sigma _0 H$ of the subgroup $H \le S_{\iota _a \sqcup \iota _b}$ of permutations fixing the $\iota _a$-summand pointwise: if $\sigma |_{\iota _a} = \sigma _0|_{\iota _a} = j$, then $\chi = \sigma _0^{-1}\sigma $ fixes the $\iota _a$-summand pointwise, and conversely. A permutation fixing the $\iota _a$-summand pointwise maps the $\iota _b$-summand into itself by injectivity, so $H \cong S_{\iota _b}$ and each fibre has cardinality $l!$.

For the sum formula, group the left-hand side by the fibres of $\sigma \mapsto \sigma |_{\iota _a}$. A non-empty fibre lies over an injective map (a restriction of an injection is injective), and then has cardinality $l!$ by the previous paragraph; over the non-injective maps both sides contribute $0$ by the hypothesis on $G$.

□
